title: Hannibal Crosses the Alps
objective: After this level you can retell Hannibal’s march over the Alps with his army and elephants.
summary: In 218 BCE Hannibal led an army with war elephants from Spain over the Alps into Italy, beginning the Second Punic War.

cards.headline: The attack Rome never expected came over the mountains, with elephants.
A general sworn against Rome
cards.body: According to tradition, Hannibal’s father made him swear as a boy never to be a friend of Rome. As a Carthaginian general based in Spain, Hannibal attacked Saguntum, a Roman ally, sparking the Second Punic War, which lasted from 218 to 201 BCE. Then he invaded Italy.

cards.headline: Over the Alps
cards.body: In 218 BCE Hannibal marched his army, including war elephants, from Spain over the Alps. The crossing cost him many men, though most of the elephants survived it, only to die in the cold soon after. But he reached Italy and began winning battles almost at once. He would stay and fight in Italy for about 15 years.

questions.prompt: Which route did Hannibal take to invade Italy?

options.label: By sea from Carthage to Ostia
Through Greece and across the Adriatic

questions.explanation: Hannibal marched from Spain over the Alps into Italy in 218 BCE.

questions.prompt: What did the Alpine crossing cost Hannibal?

options.label: His whole army
options.rationale: He reached Italy and won battles.

options.label: Many men, though most elephants survived
His command, which went to his brother

questions.explanation: The crossing cost many men, though most of the elephants survived it, only to die in the cold soon after. Hannibal still reached Italy with enough of his army to win.

questions.prompt: From Level 22: why might Hannibal have chosen to come by land rather than by sea?

options.label: Carthage had no ships at all
Rome now had a strong navy of its own

questions.explanation: After building a fleet in the First Punic War, Rome could contest the sea, so a land invasion avoided it.
